cards.text: Big day in Jerusalem, friend. Solomon, king of Israel, calls in the elders of Israel: all the tribal heads and family leaders of the Israelites. They're there to bring something up from Zion, the City of David.

cards.question: Solomon has gathered every leader in Israel. What are they there to bring up from Zion?

answers.text: The ark of the covenant of the LORD
The bronze serpent that Moses made
The sword that belonged to Goliath

cards.text: And all the men of Israel come together to King Solomon at the feast in the seventh month, the month of Ethanim. ALL of them, together. Friend, some days I can't even get one batch of dough to come together.

cards.question: Once all the elders of Israel arrive, King Solomon picks up the ark himself.

cards.text: The priests take up the ark. The priests and Levites carry up the ark of the LORD, the Tent of Meeting and all its sacred furnishings.
There, in front of the ark, King Solomon and the whole congregation of Israel start sacrificing sheep and oxen.

cards.question: Solomon and all Israel sacrifice sheep and oxen in front of the ark. How many?

answers.text: So many they could not be counted
Seven of each and no more

cards.text: Too many to COUNT. I picture one guy with a clipboard who got to forty, looked up, and just quietly sat down. Meanwhile the priests bring the ark to its place in the inner sanctuary of the temple, the Most Holy Place.

cards.question: The priests carry the ark into the Most Holy Place. Where exactly do they set it?

answers.text: Beneath the wings of the cherubim
In front of the bronze Sea

cards.text: The cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark. They overshadow the ark AND its poles. Built-in shade, friend, and my bakery can't even get an awning to stay up.

cards.question: The ark's poles are long enough that their ends can be seen from the Holy Place in front of the inner sanctuary.

cards.text: From the Holy Place, yes. From outside it, no. Now, what's actually inside that ark?

cards.question: What's inside the ark when the priests set it in the Most Holy Place?

answers.text: The tablets and a jar of manna

cards.question: Those stone tablets were placed in the ark by ___ at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with Israel after they came out of Egypt.

cards.text: The ark is in its place. Then the priests come out of the Holy Place, and I bet nobody there ever forgets what happens next.

cards.question: As the priests come out of the Holy Place, the ___ fills the house of the LORD.
With the cloud filling the house of the LORD, the priests keep right on ministering inside.
The priests can't even stand in the house of the LORD to minister. Why not?

answers.text: The glory of the LORD filled the house
Smoke from the sacrifices filled the house
The king had ordered everyone outside

cards.text: Then Solomon speaks up about that cloud. He declares: “The LORD has said that He would dwell in the thick cloud.”

cards.question: Solomon speaks to the LORD about the house he has built. What does he say it is?

answers.text: A place for You to dwell forever
A place for You to visit yearly
A place for You to rest awhile

cards.question: With the whole assembly of Israel standing there, King Solomon turns around and blesses them all.

cards.text: Solomon blesses the LORD, the God of Israel, who fulfilled with His own hand what He spoke with His mouth to Solomon's father David. His mouth said it, His hand did it, while MY mouth says "I'm up" and my hand hits snooze.
Then Solomon quotes what God told his father David, going all the way back to the day He brought Israel out of Egypt.

cards.question: God says that since He brought Israel out of Egypt, He has not chosen a city from any tribe of Israel to build a house for His Name.
God didn't choose a city. But He says He chose ___ to be over His people Israel.

cards.text: Solomon says it was in his father David's heart to build a house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

cards.question: David wanted to build a house for God's Name. What does the LORD tell David about that?

answers.text: He did well to have it in his heart
He never should have thought of it
He must wait until he is much older

cards.question: Nevertheless, David is not the one to build it. The LORD says David's ___ will build the house for His Name.

cards.text: Now, Solomon says, the LORD has fulfilled the word He spoke. Solomon has succeeded his father David, he sits on the throne of Israel, and he has built the house for the Name of the LORD.

cards.question: Solomon says he's provided a place for the ark, which holds the LORD's covenant with their fathers. When did the LORD make that covenant?

answers.text: When He brought them out of Egypt
When He gave them the Promised Land
When they crossed the Jordan River

cards.text: Friend, set this one on the cooling rack for now. This day at the temple still has more in the oven.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the verse 2 retelling, 'ALL of them, together.' and the dough joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences and two beats. One beat is the clipboard joke about verse 5. The other is the ark being brought into the Most Holy Place in verse 6.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'Meanwhile the priests bring the ark' says the two events happen at the same time. 1 Kings 8:6 says 'Then the priests brought the ark,' which puts them in order.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The joke places a modern image, a guy with a clipboard, inside the Bible scene itself. It blends the everyday comparison with the setting of the sacrifice in verse 5.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the wings, the overshadowing, and the awning joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'From the Holy Place, yes.' 'From outside it, no.' and 'Now, what's actually inside that ark?'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This is a flat retelling with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Card 5 is the same, so two plain-narration cards run back to back.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Most story cards in this stop are plain narration with no personality: cards 1, 5, 8 and 11. Card 4 has the only joke before the closing line. The stop reads like a nice dad being pleasant, not laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: 'Solomon blesses the LORD' renames what the text describes. 1 Kings 8:15 says Solomon 'said: “Blessed be the LORD...”' The card should say what Solomon said, not turn it into an act of blessing.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Earlier cards already give away this answer, 'When He brought them out of Egypt.' Stop 1 card 14 says the LORD made the covenant at Horeb 'after they came out of Egypt.' Stop 2 cards 5 and 6 also repeat the Egypt exodus. A different question is needed for verse 21.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse. It still cites 1 Kings 8:21, which choice card 12 already covered.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line, what should its 'verses' field cite? Should it repeat the last verse, or use something else?
